derivation: cos(2a) goes negative past a = pi/4, so the declared non-negativity rule fails over the upper half of the angle domain - but only where there is a speed to multiply. At v = 0 the range is -0.0, which satisfies r >= 0, so the speed is part of the region and the zero-speed edge is not. That corner is the honest reason the box names two axes. The upper bound is pi/2 to the last digit rather than 1.5708 because that is the domain edge, and `aporia-bench audit` refuses a region bound that leaves the declared domain: a box reaching past the edge cannot be checked against any point the grid will ever sample, and its fraction was being clamped to the whole axis.
expect: a band in angle, independent of speed and gravity
